sizeGuide.title: How to choose a size
sizeGuide.intro: Measure over underwear with a tape measure: snug, but not tight.
sizeGuide.chestHow: Around the fullest part, keeping the tape level under the arms.
sizeGuide.waistHow: Around the narrowest part, usually just above the navel.
sizeGuide.hipsHow: Around the fullest part of the seat, keeping the tape level.
sizeGuide.inseamHow: From the crotch to the ankle along the inside of the leg.
sizeGuide.shoesIntro: Measure in the evening — feet are slightly larger by the end of the day — wearing the socks you'll wear with the shoes. Stand on a sheet of paper and trace your foot.
sizeGuide.footLengthHow: From the heel to the tip of the longest toe. Measure both feet and go with the larger one.
sizeGuide.footWidthHow: Across the widest part, at the base of the toes.
sizeGuide.headwearIntro: Measure without a hat, using a tape measure: snug, but not pressing.
sizeGuide.head: Head circumference
sizeGuide.headHow: One finger above the eyebrows, over the ears and around the fullest part of the back of the head.
sizeGuide.doubt: Not sure? Ask the seller — they know how this model fits.

catalog.title: Catalogue
catalog.s1: All the shop’s products. Next to the price it says what it is for: a piece, a bag or a box.
catalog.s2: Like a product? Click “Add to basket”. Click the photo to open the product card.
catalog.s3: Know what you need? Click “Quick order” and add it without searching.
catalog.s4: Done choosing? Open the basket and click “Check out the request”.
catalog.r1: You see the price and what it is for: a piece, a bag or a box.
catalog.e1: “Cement M500 — 2800 per bag”. You need 20 bags — so 56,000. Why: you know the cost in advance.
catalog.d1: Next: choose a product and put it in the basket — step 2.
catalog.r2: The product goes to the basket and the number on the basket button at the top grows.
catalog.e2: “Cement M500” says “Sold in 10 kg”? Then the button adds 10 kg at once. Why: the seller sells in such portions, less can’t be ordered.
catalog.d2: Next: add the rest. Chosen everything — step 4.
catalog.r3: A field opens: type the name — the product is found and added without browsing the catalogue.
catalog.e3: You always buy the same cement — type “cement M500” and the quantity. Why: faster than scrolling the catalogue.
catalog.d3: Next: chosen everything — open the basket (step 4).
catalog.e4: The basket has 20 bags of cement and 5 buckets of paint — click “Check out the request”. Why: the seller gets the whole list at once.
catalog.d4: Next: on the checkout page choose how to get the order and send the request (the “Place your request” instruction).
catalog.next: Basket ready? Open it and check out the request.

item.title: Product
item.s1: Everything about the product: photos, price, stock and reviews.
item.s2: Choose the quantity and click “Add to basket”.
item.s3: No need to pay now. The seller checks stock and confirms the request.
item.s4: A question about the product? Click “Ask the seller”.
item.r1: You see everything needed to decide: photos, price, stock and what other customers say.
item.e1: The product has “4.7 of 5, 3 reviews” and “In stock”. Why: you can take it — it is there and people like it.
item.r2: The product goes to the basket. “Added to basket” appears at the top.
item.e2: You need 30 kg and it is sold in 10 kg — choose 30. Why: the seller picks exactly that much.
item.d2: Next: go back to the catalogue for other products or open the basket and check out.
item.r3: Money is needed only when the seller confirms everything is there.
item.e3: You sent the request in the evening, in the morning the seller answered “all in stock” — then you pay. Why: you don’t pay for what may not be there.
item.d3: Next: put the product in the basket and check out.
item.r4: A field for the question opens. The answer comes to “Questions to seller”.
item.e4: “Do you have the same in white?” — ask right here. Why: the seller knows at once which product you mean.
item.d4: Next: look for the answer in “Questions to seller”.
item.next: Put it in the basket? Open the basket and check out.

checkout.title: Place your request
checkout.s1: Your request: what is in it and what it costs.
checkout.s2: Choose how to get the order: delivery or pickup. For delivery enter the address.
checkout.s3: All correct? Click “Send the request to the seller”.
checkout.s4: No need to pay now. The seller checks stock and answers in “My requests”.
checkout.r1: You see all products, quantities and the total.
checkout.e1: “Cement M500 — 20 bags, total 56,000”. Wrong quantity — fix it here. Why: the seller picks exactly what is in the request.
checkout.d1: Next: choose how to get the order — step 2.
checkout.r2: The delivery cost is added to the total by itself.
checkout.e2: Pickup — free, you collect it. Delivery — enter “Astana, Abay St 10, flat 5”. Why: the seller knows where to deliver and calculates the cost.
checkout.d2: Next: check everything once more and send — step 3.
checkout.r3: The request goes to the seller. You see “The request has been sent”.
checkout.e3: You clicked “Send the request to the seller” — “The request has been sent” and a button to see your requests appeared. Why: now the seller checks stock.
checkout.d3: Next: wait for the seller — the request is in “My requests” with the status “Seller is checking”.
checkout.r4: The seller first checks everything is there and only then asks for payment.
checkout.e4: The seller answered there is no paint — you lost nothing because you hadn’t paid. Why: you pay only for what is surely there.
checkout.d4: Next: open “My requests” and follow the status.
checkout.next: Request sent — follow it in “My requests”.

orders.title: My requests
orders.s1: All your requests and where each one is now. On the right it explains each status.
orders.s2: See “Your answer needed”? The seller changed something. Click the request, then “Open order” — and answer: “I agree” or “Cancel”.
orders.s3: Click a request to see details. A question — click “Ask a question”.
orders.s4: Request finished and you need more? Click “Order the same again”.
orders.r1: Next to each request is its status and what you need to do.
orders.e1: “Seller is checking” — nothing to do. “Your answer needed” — the seller is waiting for you. Why: you see at once where your action is needed.
orders.d1: Next: a request shows “Your answer needed”? Step 2.
orders.r2: After “I agree” the request becomes “Accepted” — the seller starts picking.
orders.e2: The seller wrote: “No paint, a similar one for 1500”. It suits you — “I agree”. No — “Cancel”. Why: the seller won’t pick the order without your agreement.
orders.d2: Next: wait for “Ready for pickup” — then collect the order.
orders.r3: Products, total, conversation with the seller and buttons open.
orders.e3: Want delivery on Friday instead of tomorrow? Click “Ask a question” and write. Why: the seller sees the question right in this request.
orders.d3: Next: the seller’s answer appears right there in the request.
orders.r4: All products of that request are back in the basket.
orders.e4: You buy the same every week — click “Order the same again”. Why: no searching for each product again.
orders.d4: Next: check the basket and check out.
orders.next: Click a request and “Open order” — details and the reply to the seller are there.

order.title: Request
order.s1: Everything about the request: what you sent and what the seller offers.
order.s2: The seller suggested changes? Look and click “I agree”. Not suitable — “Cancel”.
order.s3: Need an invoice? Click “Download the invoice”.
order.s4: Questions about a request are asked in the list: click “To all requests”, then the request and “Ask a question”.
order.r1: You see what you sent and what the seller offers.
order.e1: You asked for 20 bags, the seller offers 18 — there are no more. Why: you see what changed.
order.d1: Next: the seller changed something? Step 2.
order.r2: After “I agree” the seller starts picking. After “Cancel” the request closes.
order.e2: The seller offered 18 bags instead of 20 — it suits you, click “I agree”. Why: the seller picks only what you agreed to.
order.r3: The invoice downloads as a file — you can send it to accounting.
order.e3: Accounting needs the invoice — click “Download the invoice” and send the file. Why: companies pay invoices from their bank account.
order.d3: Next: pay the invoice as agreed with the seller.
order.r4: The request list opens, and the request has an “Ask a question” button.
order.e4: A question “Can I pick up on Saturday?” — click “To all requests”, open the request and “Ask a question”. Why: the question is tied to this request.
order.d4: Next: the seller’s answer appears in the request.
order.next: Wait for “Ready for pickup” — then collect the order.

favorites.title: Favourites
favorites.s1: Products you marked with a heart in the catalogue.
favorites.s2: Click “Add what is available to the request” — everything in stock goes to the basket.
favorites.r1: You see the products you buy often.
favorites.e1: You hearted the cement and paint you buy every month. Why: no searching for them each time.
favorites.d1: Next: put them in the basket with one button — step 2.
favorites.r2: Everything in stock goes to the basket. What isn’t is listed.
favorites.e2: Of 5 favourites 4 are in stock, 1 ran out — 4 go to the basket. Why: fast, and nothing extra.
favorites.d2: Next: open the basket and check out.
favorites.next: Open the basket and check out.

promotions.title: Offers and discounts
promotions.s2: The discount is applied in the basket automatically — nothing to enter.
promotions.s3: There is an offer? Click the “See…” button under it — discounted products open.
promotions.r1: You see all discounts running now.
promotions.e1: For example, a sale on some products and a first-order discount. Why: you know where to save.
promotions.r2: The discount shows in the basket — the price is already reduced.
promotions.e2: A product cost 1000, with a 3% discount the basket shows 970. Why: nothing to enter, no promo codes.
promotions.d2: Next: put products in the basket and check out.
promotions.e3: You clicked the button under the offer — only those products show. Why: no searching the whole catalogue for discounts.
promotions.d3: Next: put what you need in the basket.
promotions.next: Choose discounted products and check out.

templates.title: Templates
templates.s1: A template is a saved basket. Handy if you often order the same things.
templates.s2: Need your last order? Click “Repeat the previous order”.
templates.s3: To save the basket, enter a name in “Save the current basket” and click “Save”.
templates.s4: Next time click “To the basket” on the template — everything is added at once.
templates.e1: Template “Cement for the site”: 20 bags of cement and 5 buckets of paint. Why: no rebuilding the same basket every time.
templates.d1: Next: repeat the previous order (step 2) or save the basket (step 3).
templates.r2: Products from your last order are in the basket.
templates.e2: You ordered the same a month ago — click “Repeat the previous order”. Why: one button instead of searching.
templates.d2: Next: check the basket and check out.
templates.r3: The template appears in the list.
templates.e3: Name “Weekly order” — “Save”. Why: next time it takes one click.
templates.r4: All template products are in the basket.
templates.e4: On the “Weekly order” template click “To the basket”. Why: the request is ready in a second.
templates.d4: Next: open the basket and check out.
templates.next: Basket ready — check out the request.

questions.title: Questions to seller
questions.s1: Your conversation with the seller: about products, timing and delivery.
questions.s2: Type your question in the “Write a message” field and press the send button.
questions.s3: You can also ask about a product on its card — with “Ask the seller”.
questions.s4: The seller’s answer appears right here.
questions.r1: You see all questions and the seller’s answers.
questions.e1: Yesterday you asked about delivery — the answer is already here. Why: the conversation isn’t lost.
questions.r2: The question goes to the seller, marked as waiting for the seller’s answer.
questions.e2: “Can you deliver on Saturday?” — write and send. Why: the seller answers right here.
questions.d2: Next: wait for the answer — it appears right here (step 4).
questions.r3: The question is about a specific product — the seller knows what you mean.
questions.e3: On the paint’s card click “Ask the seller”: “Is there white?”. Why: no explaining which product.
questions.d3: Next: the answer comes here, to “Questions to seller”.
questions.r4: The seller’s answer appears next to the question.
questions.e4: The seller answered: “Yes, we deliver on Saturday”. Why: everything in one place.
questions.d4: Next: you can place a request in the catalogue.
questions.next: Got the answer? Place a request in the catalogue.

reviews.title: My reviews
reviews.s2: Other customers see a review once the seller publishes it.
reviews.s3: You can edit or delete a review.
reviews.r1: You see your reviews and their status.
reviews.e1: The cement review is already published, the paint review is still being checked by the seller. Why: you see what others already see.
reviews.d1: Next: step 2 — how a review reaches others.
reviews.r2: Until the seller checks it, only you see the review.
reviews.e2: You wrote a review in the evening — in the morning the seller published it. Why: reviews have no ads or rudeness.
reviews.d2: Next: if needed — edit the review (step 3).
reviews.r3: An edited review goes back for checking.
reviews.e3: You first gave 3 stars, then the seller fixed everything — change it to 5. Why: the review honestly reflects the purchase.
reviews.next: Rate other products you bought — it helps other customers.

delivery.title: Delivery and pickup
delivery.s1: All the ways to get your order: delivery and pickup.
delivery.s2: Each way shows what you will be asked at checkout — for example, the address.
delivery.s3: Choose the pickup point at the top of the page — it shows what is in stock.
delivery.r1: You see how you can get the order.
delivery.e1: “Pickup — free” and “City delivery — 3000”. Why: you choose in advance.
delivery.d1: Next: see what you’ll be asked at checkout — step 2.
delivery.r2: You know in advance what to prepare.
delivery.e2: For delivery you’re asked the address and floor. Why: everything is at hand at checkout.
delivery.d2: Next: choose a pickup point — step 3.
delivery.r3: The catalogue shows stock at exactly this point.
delivery.e3: You chose “Abay warehouse” — the catalogue shows what is there. Why: you won’t come for what this warehouse doesn’t have.
delivery.d3: Next: choose products in the catalogue.
delivery.next: Chose a way — go to the catalogue for products.

profile.title: Suppliers
profile.s2: Buying for a company? Click “Fill in details”, enter the data and click “Save”. The seller issues the VAT invoice to it.
profile.s3: Your consents are in “Personal data consents”.
profile.r1: You see the shops you buy from.
profile.e1: “Roza LLP — selected”. Why: you can switch to another shop.
profile.d1: Next: buying for a company? Step 2.
profile.r2: “Details saved” appears. The VAT invoice is issued to the company.
profile.e2: Bereke LLP, BIN 123456789012, address. Why: accounting will accept the documents.
profile.r3: You can download the consent document.
profile.e3: Need a copy of the consent — click “Download PDF”. Why: you have the document.
profile.next: Back to the catalogue for shopping.

ordersAnswer.title: My requests: needs your answer
ordersAnswer.s1: Requests where the seller changed something and waits for you.
ordersAnswer.e1: The seller wrote: “No paint, a similar one for 1500”. Why: without your answer the seller won’t pick the order.
ordersAnswer.s2: Click the request, then “Open order”, and answer: “I agree” or “Cancel”.
ordersAnswer.r2: After “I agree” the request becomes “Accepted” and moves to “With the seller”.
ordersAnswer.e2: The similar paint suits you — “I agree”. Why: the seller starts picking at once.
ordersAnswer.next: Answered? Follow the request in “With the seller”.

ordersReady.title: My requests: ready for pickup
ordersReady.s1: Picked requests — you can collect them.
ordersReady.r1: Each says “Needed: collect from the shop” and the address.
ordersReady.e1: The request is picked, the shop is at Kabanbay Batyr 43. Why: you know where to go.
ordersReady.d1: Next: come for the order — step 2.
ordersReady.s2: At the shop give the pickup code — it is in the request.
ordersReady.r2: The seller hands over the order and the request moves to “Received”.
ordersReady.e2: You gave code 4821 — you got 20 bags. Why: the code protects your order from others.
ordersReady.next: Collected the order? Rate the purchase — it helps other customers.

ordersSeller.title: My requests: with the seller
ordersSeller.s1: Requests the seller is working on.
ordersSeller.r1: It says “Nothing to do — waiting for the seller” or “— we’re picking the request”.
ordersSeller.e1: The request is “Accepted” — the seller is picking. Why: you see you’re not forgotten.
ordersSeller.d1: Next: wait. When the seller answers or picks it, the request moves to “Needs your answer” or “Ready for pickup”.
ordersSeller.s2: A question? Click the request and “Ask a question”.
ordersSeller.r2: The seller sees the question right in this request.
ordersSeller.e2: “Can I pick up on Saturday?”. Why: no need to call.
ordersSeller.d2: Next: the answer appears in the request.
ordersSeller.next: Wait — the status changes by itself.

ordersDone.title: My requests: received
ordersDone.r1: You can rate the purchase or order the same again.
ordersDone.e1: The cement was good — rate it. Why: other customers learn about quality.
ordersDone.s2: Click the request and “Order the same again”.
ordersDone.r2: All products go to the basket.
ordersDone.e2: You buy the same every month — one button. Why: no searching again.
ordersDone.d2: Next: open the basket and check out.
ordersDone.next: Repeated? Open the basket and check out.

ordersCancelled.title: My requests: cancelled
ordersCancelled.s1: Requests cancelled by you or the seller.
ordersCancelled.e1: You cancelled because you found the product closer. Why: the history is kept.
ordersCancelled.d1: Next: changed your mind — order again in the catalogue.
ordersCancelled.next: Need a product? Open the catalogue.

questionsArchive.title: Questions: WhatsApp archive
questionsArchive.s1: All your WhatsApp conversation with the shop — even if it was deleted from your phone.
questionsArchive.r1: It is an archive: you can’t reply here.
questionsArchive.e1: Want to find the price quoted last month — it is here. Why: nothing gets lost.
questionsArchive.d1: Next: to write to the seller — the “Questions to the seller” tab.
questionsArchive.next: To write to the seller, open the “Questions to the seller” tab.

steps.cart: Put a product in the basket
steps.send: Send the request to the seller
